slides.headline: 6 AI POWERS YOU KEEP PAYING FOR AND IGNORING
slides.image_prompt: Sam Altman waist-up gleeful at bright neon market stall, lifts golden tray of six icons—chart, magnifying glass, chip, microphone, binder, robot—toward outstretched hand. OpenAI symbol on banner, studio light, natural skin, bright teal.

slides.headline: 1) UPLOAD YOUR ENTIRE P&L TO CHATGPT
slides.body: A CFO charges $400/hr for this. It's free inside your ChatGPT plan right now. "Here is my P&L. Find my 5 biggest cost leaks and rank them by dollar amount."
slides.image_prompt: Sam Altman, fierce focus, waist-up in a bright green accountant visor, red marker mid-circle on an enormous glowing spreadsheet grid — red downward arrows and loss symbols only, no readable text. Vivid emerald overhead lamp blazing. OpenAI logo exactly as in the reference image glows on the far wall. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, natural skin texture, slight film grain. Accent: signal red on saturated emerald.

slides.headline: 2) TURN ON CHATGPT MEMORY FOR YOUR BUSINESS
slides.body: ChatGPT Plus has Memory. Most users never switch it on, so every chat starts from scratch. "Remember: I run a [business type]. My best customers care about [X]. Always lead with [Y]."
slides.image_prompt: Sam Altman, wide-eyed satisfaction, waist-up in a grease-marked mechanic jumpsuit, presses a glowing amber brain-shaped chip into the chest panel of a white boxy robot — robot eyes igniting electric green in real time. OpenAI logo exactly as in the reference image on the robot chest. Bright steel-blue industrial garage, blazing overhead work lamps. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, natural skin texture, slight film grain. Accent: electric green on steel blue.

slides.headline: 3) PASTE YOUR ENTIRE VENDOR CONTRACT INTO CLAUDE
slides.body: Lawyers charge $500/hr to review contracts. Your Claude account reads 200,000 words at once, free. "Here is my vendor contract. Flag every clause that could cost me money or limit my options."

slides.headline: 4) LET CHATGPT BROWSE YOUR COMPETITOR'S WEBSITE LIVE
slides.body: A market research firm charges $2,000 for a competitor brief. ChatGPT browses live and writes one free. "Go to [competitor website]. List their pricing, main promises, and 3 weaknesses I can beat."

slides.headline: 5) BUILD A CLAUDE PROJECT THAT KNOWS YOUR WHOLE BUSINESS
slides.body: A Claude Project remembers every document you upload. It acts like a team member who never forgets. "You are my support rep. Use the documents I uploaded to answer customer questions. Never guess."

slides.headline: 6) REHEARSE YOUR HARDEST SALES CALL WITH CHATGPT VOICE
slides.body: Sales coaches charge $300/hr. ChatGPT's voice mode argues back in real time, for free. "Act as a skeptical buyer. I sell [product]. Push back hard on my price. Let's roleplay."

pinned_comment: Which of these did you already know about? Most people I show these to have found maybe 1 of the 6. The contract review on slide 4 is the one that usually stops people cold.

candidates: YOUR COMPETITORS ARE USING 6 CHATGPT POWERS YOU HAVEN'T FOUND
YOUR CHATGPT SUBSCRIPTION HAS 6 POWERS YOU'VE NEVER USED
hook_tournament.why: [1] hits your wallet immediately—you already PAY for this, so 'you're not using it' feels like wasted money. [0] needs you to care about competitors first, which is an extra mental step a 2am scroller won't take.

candidates: YOUR CHATGPT SUBSCRIPTION HAS 6 POWERS YOU'VE NEVER USED
6 EXPENSIVE SERVICES YOUR AI SUBSCRIPTION ALREADY REPLACES
6 AI POWERS YOU KEEP PAYING FOR AND IGNORING
hook_sharpen.why: The accusatory 'YOU KEEP PAYING FOR AND IGNORING' lands like a personal call-out that makes you stop—it stings a little and you *have* to check. [1] is smarter (value play) but colder; [0] sounds like every other generic feature list.
